deep.reconstruction:
This page has no mathematics. It is a draft, with several layers of revision, of the opening paragraph of Riemann's paper 'Ein Beitrag zu den Untersuchungen über die Bewegung eines gleichartigen flüssigen Ellipsoids' (Abh. Ges. Wiss. Göttingen 9, 1861). There are no formulas and no derivations.

Layers:
(a) A pencil heading: 'Über die Bewegung eines flüssigen gleichartigen Ellipsoids.'
(b) Faint pencil sketches of the programme. The first, abandoned, begins 'Die Untersuchungen über ein flüssiges homogenes Ellipsoid, dessen einzelne ...'. A second speaks of gathering Dirichlet's investigation into a larger circle of results. A third aims to make the differential equations independent of the chosen initial instant. This is to be done by posing the problem for the axes of the ellipsoid and the velocities parallel to them. A further pencil remark notes that the problem of the rotation of a rigid body 'is known to' lead to reducing this task to quadratures. Here Riemann compares his reduction to the Euler-Poinsot rigid-body problem.
(c) An ink trial sentence: 'I will refer to Dirichlet's paper, but it was not possible to keep its notation unchanged.'
(d) The title in ink: 'Ein Beitrag zu den Untersuchungen über die Bewegung eines gleichartigen flüssigen Ellipsoids v. B. Riemann.'
(e) The ink paragraph that, with small changes, became the printed introduction. Its content:
- Dirichlet, in his last paper (edited by Dedekind), broke new ground on the motion of a homogeneous fluid ellipsoid whose elements attract by the law of gravitation.
- The subject is mathematically attractive apart from the question of the figures of celestial bodies.
- Dirichlet carried the solution through completely only in the simplest cases.
- For further work it is useful to give the differential equations a form independent of the initial instant.
- This can be done by asking how the principal axes of the ellipsoid and the relative motion of the fluid with respect to them change. The final line is the replacement clause for a struck passage: 'die Grösse der Hauptaxen ... und die relative Bewegung der flüssigen Masse gegen dieselben sich ändert'.
- Dirichlet's paper is presupposed, but its notation could not be kept.

Context (my addition, not on the page): Dirichlet takes particle positions linear in the initial positions, x(t) = P(t) a, i.e. a homogeneous deformation. Incompressibility forces det P to be constant. Riemann's later decomposition P = S·diag(a1,a2,a3)·T, with S and T rotations, separates the shape and orientation of the ellipsoid from the internal motion. That decomposition is the 'initial-instant-independent' formulation announced here; it is not carried out on this page.
errors: No mathematical content, so no mathematical errors. The prose contains drafting slips typical of a working draft: struck phrases, an unfinished clause ('auf welche ...') whose completion appears at the bottom of the page, and duplicated statements about notation.

results.what: Programmatic statement: reformulate Dirichlet's equations for the self-gravitating homogeneous fluid ellipsoid so they are independent of the initial instant, by describing the evolution of the principal axes and of the fluid's motion relative to them.
results.modern_name: Riemann's formulation of Dirichlet's problem (Riemann ellipsoids, Dirichlet-Dedekind-Riemann theory; cf. Chandrasekhar, Ellipsoidal Figures of Equilibrium)

results.what: Remark comparing the reduction to quadratures with the rigid-body rotation problem
results.modern_name: Analogy with the Euler-Poinsot top / integrable reduction
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann 1861 (the analogy appears in the published paper)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of the published introduction of Riemann's 1861 ellipsoid paper, matching the printed text closely. It contains no mathematics beyond the well-known announced programme.

checkable.asserts: (My context, not on the page) In Dirichlet's linear ansatz x=P(t)a, the ellipsoid's squared semi-axes are the eigenvalues of P P^T (up to scaling). Their product equals det(P)^2, so constant volume and density is det P = const.

transcription_corrections: The final line is not a free sentence. It is the replacement completing the struck clause 'auf welche ...': roughly '... dass man die Aufgabe aufstellt, [zu bestimmen, wie sich] die Grösse der Hauptaxen des Ellipsoids und die relative Bewegung der flüssigen Masse gegen dieselben ändert.'
In the pencil line 'einen größeren[?] Kreis[?] zusammenzufassen' the reading is uncertain. The sense is to embrace Dirichlet's investigation in a wider framework.

The pencil line ending '... Rotation eines festen Körpers ist bekanntlich führen' is better read as a remark that the rigid-body rotation problem is known to reduce to quadratures, with Riemann's problem reduced analogously ('diese Aufgabe auf Quadraturen zurückzuführen').
'nach dem Gesetz der Schwere': 'Schwere' is an interlinear replacement for a struck word. The printed version speaks of the Newtonian law of attraction.
The struck word before 'Abhandlung' in the trial sentence is uncertain ('Bemerkung' is doubtful); it may be another noun such as 'Darstellung'.
